subject: Recap + next steps: Aurabound pilot launch guardrails and deliverables
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@aurabound.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@aurabound.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: Aurabound pilot launch guardrails and deliverables

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive conversation today. Quick recap of what we heard from your team and the plan we discussed for a focused pilot. I captured the pieces so we have a single source of truth before we lock dates.

Top pain points you shared
- Latency spikes when routing multi-turn queries to your classification service (~450–600ms tail) impacting UX on mobile.
- Cost of current token-based scoring pipeline when processing high-volume batched requests.
- Lack of reliable regression monitoring for prompt-level accuracy during model updates.

Pilot goals (success criteria)
1) Reduce median generation latency for the 95th percentile by 25% for the targeted classification route.
2) Demonstrate a 20% reduction in per-request inference cost using Redwood batching + prefix KV caching without degrading golden-set accuracy (target: within ±2% F1).
3) Run a prompt evaluation suite (200 examples) and establish a baseline so we can surface regressions automatically on rollout.

Scope & deliverables (what Redwood will deliver)
- Pilot environment: hosted dedicated lane for the classification route with a single model variant and a fallback.
- Observability: token-level cost dashboard, 95/99 latency slices, and prompt eval runbook.
- Prompt set & evals: Redwood will onboard the initial 200-case prompt suite and run an A/B against your current model using your golden labels.
- Access & setup: temporary service account + S3 read-only sample data drop, plus a short SSH window for the integration engineer if needed.

Owners & roles
- Aurabound: Alex (technical lead), Priya (product owner), procurement (contracts).
- Redwood: Marissa (AE / engagement lead), Ben Carter (Solutions Engineer / integration lead), Jordan Blake (Customer Success / metrics and runbook).

Timeline (draft)
- Week 0 (this week): sign the SOW + NDA (procurement touchpoint).
- Week 1: environment provisioning, RBAC + service account, data sample upload.
- Week 2: model routing + batching config; run initial smoke tests.
- Week 3–4: prompt eval runs and performance tuning; compile final baseline report.

Immediate asks for Aurabound
1) Procurement contact to review the SOW we attached (procurement@aurabound.ai).
2) A sample of 10–20 representative conversations (PII redacted) in the agreed S3 layout.
3) Confirmation of the golden-label owners for the 200-case prompt set.

Attachments: pilot charter (PDF), access checklist (CSV). Link to the draft SOW in HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/4821

If that matches what you expect, we’ll move to SOW execution and lock Week 1 provisioning on Monday 7/5.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Alex Dunn <alex.dunn@aurabound.ai>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@aurabound.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Aurabound pilot launch guardrails and deliverables

Marissa —

Thanks for pulling this together so quickly. High level: this aligns with what we discussed. A few notes and clarifications from our side:

- The 200-case prompt set looks right; Priya and I will nominate the golden-label owners (likely Sarah on Product and Omar on Data Ops). We’ll confirm names by EOD Friday 7/2.
- We can provide a sanitized 15-conversation sample in S3 by Monday 7/5. We’ll use the Redaction template you linked.
- Regarding the SSH window: we prefer to avoid direct SSH if possible. Can Ben confirm whether the integration can be completed via API keys and temporary IAM role instead?

We started an internal procurement thread; procurement@aurabound.ai will review the SOW. If they ask for any changes, we’ll loop you in immediately.

One ask for Redwood: can you include the expected cost delta at the projected throughput (400 qps) in the SOW appendix? That will help our finance team speed approval.

—Alex
Alex Dunn
Head of Product (AI)
Aurabound
alex.dunn@aurabound.ai

Alex / team —

Thanks — quick answers to the integration notes:
- We can absolutely avoid SSH. Integration will be by temporary IAM role + API key. I’ll send a minimal-runbook that covers role creation, least-privilege scopes, and the sample S3 layout.
- I’ll include a preliminary cost delta estimate at 400 qps in the appendix of the SOW; that will be a conservative operating estimate assuming your mix of short (<=64 tokens) and medium (<=256 tokens) requests.
- For the prompt evals we’ll need a mapping file for labels (CSV) and a preferred metric (you mentioned F1 — if there are class-weighting rules, send those over).

I attached the integration runbook and a lightweight config template we use for batching thresholds.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: aurabound-access-checklist.csv, integration-runbook-v1.md

Alex / Priya —

Looping in a few operational checkpoints from the CS side so nothing blocks Week 1 provisioning:
- Please confirm the S3 bucket name and the account ID that will own the sample data drop. We prefer the bucket to be in us-west-2 to reduce egress ops.
- If there are data residency or retention constraints, indicate them now so we can set TTLs on caches and confirm with security.
- We’ll schedule a 30-min onboarding session for your analytics owner during Week 1 to walk through the dashboards and the prompt-eval report format. Please propose 3 time windows (PST).

Once procurement confirms SOW redlines, Marissa / Ben will get provisioning scheduled.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.
